items.title: Harold Ousley interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: my first musical role models and heroes were Gene Ammons... I used to get a chance to go hear him a lot. So it was a lot of inspiration there.

ctx.x: You had a pretty good experience in school? With school music when you grew up?

Yeah, well I started music in high school. What happened, I went to Willard Grammar School, and before we went to high school when we were in eighth grade they sent over, the high school, DuSable, sent over applications to ask what — to let you know what subject they had and find out what subjects you wanted to be in. And so I got into band because prior to that, when I was in grammar school, I used to take piano. Because my mother gave me — my grandmother gave me piano lessons. Because at that time, to play…

all the big band things, the records for me, at the time. And so that’s when I first heard the saxophone. Of course I fell in love with it. So going to high school I wanted to get in the band and learn how to play saxophone. And Walter Dyett, a very wonderful teacher who taught Gene Ammons and Nat King Cole and people like this. First if you were going to play saxophone you had to play clarinet. And the reason for this is that a clarinet has three registers. And within it it has a saxophone register. So if you…
